searchText: Hey <@543900561460822016> & <@194432762315407360> is it okay for us to use solidity (instead of geas) for the PQ registrations EIP, at least initially? https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12609 I don't know if it's worth the hassle of porting it right now. Asking you two because you're the system contract experts 🙂 is there some special reason to do solidity? is it just the standard queue style system contract? I think it was just simpler to make the changes. I copied them from https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts/tree/main/contracts/src which <@774033563732541451> made. It should be fairly standard, though I think some fee mechanism changes were made (by potuz) to allow lots of requests before a fork enabled the consumption of them. Not totally sure to be honest. imo i would just use the sys-asm contracts, it's very easy to allow requests before the fork If needed, my closed spec from back in september directly relates to this pr. Happy to help if needed Yeah it's the same thing just in solidity & with a proof of possession check. <@774033563732541451> could we look into porting your PQ registration system contracts into https://github.com/ethereum/sys-asm next week? Then we can use that in the EIP. Sure, I can look into doing this next week. My first contract was geas and it was kinda simple to read I think the problem was when they added the signature verification which can be a bit oh sorry i didn't realize you were doing a signature verification why do you need to do that? It’s necessary to prevent someone from front-running your registration. And we don’t want to save the signature & do the signature check in the CL. I see I would do the sig verification in solidity if you want and call it from the sys-asm bc the queue part is nearly identical to the previous ones I like that idea 👍 Sounds good. I'll take that direction then. I'll ping here next week whenever i've some news about it.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: is there some special reason to do solidity? is it just the standard queue style system contract?

excerpts.content: I think it was just simpler to make the changes. I copied them from https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts/tree/main/contracts/src which <@774033563732541451> made.

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: It should be fairly standard, though I think some fee mechanism changes were made (by potuz) to allow lots of requests before a fork enabled the consumption of them. Not totally sure to be honest.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: imo i would just use the sys-asm contracts, it's very easy to allow requests before the fork

excerpts.content: If needed, my closed spec from back in september directly relates to this pr. Happy to help if needed

excerpts.content: Yeah it's the same thing just in solidity & with a proof of possession check. <@774033563732541451> could we look into porting your PQ registration system contracts into https://github.com/ethereum/sys-asm next week? Then we can use that in the EIP.
